standard_prerequisites.name: The Mittag-Leffler condition and its behaviour under quotients
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a quotient system of a Mittag-Leffler system is Mittag-Leffler and the exactness statement for limits, applied three times in the course of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mittag-Leffler along a short exact sequence with essentially constant quotient
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the Mittag-Leffler property for the system of cocycles, deduced from the Mittag-Leffler sub-system and the essentially constant quotient system that the hypothesis provides.

standard_prerequisites.name: Limits commute with kernels
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the standard identification of the limit of the kernels with the kernel of the limit
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of the limit of the cocycle systems as the cocycles of the limit complex.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 8042-8046): the author writes the cocycle systems and the boundary systems of the given inverse system of complexes and notes that the limit of the cocycle systems in degree zero is the kernel of the limit map, since taking kernels commutes with taking limits.
Mittag-Leffler for the boundaries (proof lines 8047-8052): the systems of boundaries are quotients of the two given Mittag-Leffler systems, hence are themselves Mittag-Leffler.

Mittag-Leffler for the middle cocycles (proof lines 8053-8060): the short exact sequence relating boundaries, cocycles and cohomology in degree minus one has a Mittag-Leffler sub-system and an essentially constant quotient, so the system of cocycles is Mittag-Leffler by the preceding card's lemma.

The sequence of limits (proof lines 8061-8071): the exact sequence relating the cocycles in degree minus one, the middle term and the boundaries in degree zero, together with the Mittag-Leffler lemma, shows first that the limit of the middle term surjects onto the limit of the boundaries, and then that the sequence of limits of boundaries, cocycles and cohomology in degree zero is exact; putting the identifications together gives the claimed equality.
proof_roadmap: Write the cocycles and boundaries of the system and of the limit complex.
Get Mittag-Leffler for the boundary systems as quotients of Mittag-Leffler systems.
Get Mittag-Leffler for the middle cocycles from the essentially constant quotient.
Apply the limit statement twice to identify the limit of the zeroth cohomology.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the zeroth cohomology of the limit of an inverse system of complexes with the limit of the zeroth cohomologies, assuming Mittag-Leffler conditions on the two leftmost systems and essential constancy of the first cohomology system (statement lines 8026-8039). The proof is a complete argument: the systems of boundaries are quotients of the given Mittag-Leffler systems and hence Mittag-Leffler (proof lines 8047-8052); the system of cocycles in degree minus one is Mittag-Leffler by the short exact sequence with essentially constant quotient (proof lines 8053-8060); and two applications of the limit statement for short exact sequences of inverse systems give the required identification of the limit of the zeroth cohomology (proof lines 8061-8071). The non-formal content is the arrangement of the three short exact sequences. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
